decisions.reason: It is very close to the firm’s core airport-operations software and integration capabilities, remained prominently marketed in both years, and fits the firm’s move toward automated, data-driven turnaround optimisation.

The module builds directly on the firm’s established apron and systems-integration knowledge, and its promotion from a mention to a dedicated page suggests the firm has learned enough from early adoption to continue developing it.

Although billing software is somewhat less central than operational control products, it still leverages the firm’s airport data integration base and gained visibility in 2024, so the most likely choice is to retain it rather than exit.

Apron equipment monitoring is highly complementary to the firm’s installed-equipment experience, maintenance services, and analytics capabilities, making it a strong candidate for continued improvement and commercialization.
